key_insight: Ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM) substantially boosts the hardness and wear/corrosion-related performance of WC–Co–Cr thermal spray coatings, but the best spraying route depends on the failure mode.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical steel components, pairing thermal spraying with UNSM can extend service life, yet coating selection should be matched to whether the main concern is abrasive wear, friction, cavitation, or valve endurance.
method: Deposited WC–Co–Cr coatings by detonation spraying (DS), HVOF, and APS.
Applied ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM) to each coating condition.
Evaluated microstructure and performance using SEM/EDS, hardness, tribology, abrasion, erosion, impact-abrasion, cavitation, corrosion, oxidation, and valve endurance tests.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports clear performance shifts after UNSM, including hardness increases up to 1596 HV and the best wear-test results for APS+UNSM, while HVOF+UNSM gave the best valve endurance response.
watch_item: Performance gains are mechanism-specific, so the most improved coating in lab wear tests may not be the best choice for valve service or other real operating conditions.
paper_title: Ultrasonic Surface Modification of WC-Co-Cr Thermal Spray Coatings: Microstructure, Mechanical Properties and Performance
